ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a horizontal rectangle ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left. The cut line inside the rectangle goes vertically downward from a certain point on the top side, then horizontally to the right for a segment, the horizontal segment is labeled y, and then vertically downward to the bottom side; this broken line divides the 8×18 rectangle into two congruent hexagons. Reasoning: Let the horizontal length along the top side from D to the first vertical cut line be a, the downward length of the first vertical cut line be b, and the length of the middle horizontal cut line be y. Since the second vertical cut line is y to the right of the first vertical cut line, the horizontal length along the bottom side from A to the second vertical cut line is a+y. The two hexagons are congruent, and the vertical side length 8 on the left outer side corresponds to the vertical side length 8 on the right outer side, so the adjacent horizontal parts correspond in the opposite order, giving a=18-a-y, that is, 2a+y=18. The two vertical cut-line segments also correspond to each other, so b=8-b, giving b=4. Thus each hexagon can be regarded as being composed of one strip of height 4 and length a and one strip of height 4 and length a+y. The total area of the two hexagons is the area of the original rectangle, 8·18=144, and the side length of the reassembled square is 12. The four strips of height 4 must be laid into the three layers of height 4 of the 12×12 square, so the long strip must exactly fill one layer, hence a+y=12. Solving a+y=12 together with 2a+y=18, subtracting gives a=6, and substituting back gives y=6.

method.method_draft: Introduce variables from the displayed cut: let a be the top-left horizontal segment from D to the first vertical cut, let b be the upper vertical drop, and let the middle horizontal cut be y. The lower-left bottom segment is then a+y. Use congruence of the two hexagons: the left outer vertical side of length 8 corresponds to the right outer vertical side, so adjacent horizontal pieces must match in reverse order, giving a = 18 - a - y, hence 2a + y = 18; the two vertical cut portions must also match, so b = 8 - b = 4. Thus each hexagon is a two-level stair shape made from a 4-by-a strip and a 4-by-(a+y) strip. From the text, the two pieces form a square of area 8·18 = 144, so the square side is 12. Since the two congruent stair pieces have four 4-high strips total and must tile three 4-high layers of a 12-by-12 square, the long strip must span a full layer: a+y = 12. Combine a+y = 12 with 2a+y = 18 to get a = 6 and y = 6.

一个六边形的周长为 (a+y)+4+y+4+a+8=2a+2y+16。由 2a+y=18，可得 2a=18-y，所以一个六边形周长为 18-y+2y+16=34+y。两个六边形周长总和为 68+2y。

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is a horizontal rectangle ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left. The cut line inside the rectangle goes vertically downward from a certain point on the top side, then horizontally to the right for a segment, the horizontal segment is labeled y, and then vertically downward to the bottom side; this broken line divides the 8×18 rectangle into two congruent hexagons.

Reasoning: Let the horizontal length along the top side from D to the first vertical cut line be a, the downward length of the first vertical cut line be b, and the length of the middle horizontal cut line be y. Since the second vertical cut line is y to the right of the first vertical cut line, the horizontal length along the bottom side from A to the second vertical cut line is a+y. The two hexagons are congruent, and the vertical side length 8 on the left outer side corresponds to the vertical side length 8 on the right outer side, so the adjacent horizontal parts correspond in the opposite order, giving a=18-a-y, that is, 2a+y=18. The two vertical cut-line segments also correspond to each other, so b=8-b, giving b=4. Thus each hexagon can be regarded as being composed of one strip of height 4 and length a and one strip of height 4 and length a+y. The total area of the two hexagons is the area of the original rectangle, 8·18=144, and the side length of the reassembled square is 12. The four strips of height 4 must be laid into the three layers of height 4 of the 12×12 square, so the long strip must exactly fill one layer, hence a+y=12. Solving a+y=12 together with 2a+y=18, subtracting gives a=6, and substituting back gives y=6.
